Mydei was destined to die today; He had come to terms with such a fate, long long ago.

A sacrifice foretold by prophecy, and as the sirens got bolder, more desperate in their war with the sailors of their small kingdom - food dwindling; Mydei's life was to come to an end. A sacrificial lamb being ushered into the slaughter as his body tilted along each passing wave. 

His hands bound, tightly, rope burning into his skin, and marking him in a deep crimson to match the tattoos along his body. It didn’t matter anyway that he was completely tied up - He was forbidden from water his entire life so that he may never learn to swim before this day regardless.

The pile of jewels on top of him didn’t aid any desires to swim either - It would hasten his sinking even if he thrashed.

No.

His life would end today - Either claimed by the sirens as a worthy sacrifice, or left to rot at the bottom of the ocean and consumed by the creatures there; Forgotten by all beneath the rolling tides.

He could do nothing more than sit there and let the waves rock him to sleep, the crash of waves against the vessel his last quiet lullaby.  

He had no idea how long he slept, ebbing in and out of the clutches of slumber constantly until one of the couriers to his doom spoke to him loudly; “We’re nearing your last stop, boy.”

Rasp, gruff, and hoarse sounding voice. A sorrow that it was one of the last voices Mydei would ever hear, yet, Mydei could only stare at the man in reply due to the makeshift gag of rope in his own mouth, golden eyes blinking rather slowly over the news. That was fine. The quicker it happened, the faster he would truly be able to fall asleep eternally. He would be home soon; Tucked away at the bottom of abyssal depths for forever lull him to sleep.

Golden eyes moved to stare at the wooden walls inside the ship’s captain’s quarters, it wasn’t much to look at. The vessel was tiny, purposefully so to avoid any and all eyes focusing on the fact they had the crown prince sacrifice aboard it with jewels and gold attached to him. The inside was scorchingly hot, no windows lest someone see Mydei, and the inability to move had only aided in his sweating.

Being drowned could not come fast enough if sitting here sweating piles was the other option.

The next time the door slammed open to allow the smell of the sea into the room two hefty men latched onto Mydei at the side of the entrance, lifting him with practiced ease. As if the jewels and his own body weight were nothing to the both of them; A waste of their space and time, even though he was quite sure his father was paying them handsomely for this.

“It’s your lucky day,” Mydei really doubted that. He was wearing extremely heavy jewelry all over, tied with ropes, didn’t know how to swim at all, and was being thrown into the ocean. Most people would argue that’s the opposite of a lucky day, in his experience and opinion. 

“A siren is waiting nearby. Maybe it’ll have mercy and bite your head off before you drown!”

Ah. 

They were mocking him. 

Everyone here knew he was going to die, anyway.

Mydei could do little more than huff out one of his last breaths of air in his annoyance as he knit his brows, staring at the wood beneath them as they unceremoniously carried him to the edge of the boat. 

“Look ‘ere. It’s watching us.”

Mydei did look up at that, eyes scanning the ocean waves curiously to see what a ‘siren’ even looked like. He could only blink over the sight he found, translucent scales that lined his cheeks, fins on the side of his face replacing ears of a shiny pale blue, eyes sharp - Almost predatory as they met Mydei’s. 

Mydei could only blink at the horrific sight, the terror that was a ‘siren’, and the fact they were so very pretty. Mydei had never seen one, due to the whole ‘forbidden to go near pools of water so he doesn’t learn to swim’ thing, but now he couldn’t quite grasp the way everyone wrote them as terrifying monsters. 

If anything, as Mydei stared in pure wander over that creature - It looked petrified staring right back at him, Mydei even swore it opened his mouth at him as if to say something before he tore his eyes away from it. Perhaps it was going to sing a song that would burrow into their minds and haunt them - It mattered not to Mydei, however.

“Well, off you go then.” 

Mydei felt himself scoff at that, as much as he could through rope as he fully lowered his gaze from the almost panic-stricken appearing siren, instead faltering to watching the wood rock by. Watching it almost in a trance as they swung him back and forth a few times for momentum, before flinging him off the railing easily.

The sharp pitched shrill noise that rang into his ears as he was thrown overboard almost immediately made his head feel as though it was threatening to crack open. That worry faded swifty, anyway.

As Mydei crashed into the water, and sank beneath the tide easily - terribly fast due to the practical weights on him, that terrible skull-splintering headache became his last issue. Instead he couldn’t help but notice how nice it was beneath the waves - Eerily peacefully silent as he fell to the ocean’s depths.

Mydei held his breath - He wasn’t sure why, but he did. Maybe it was simply so he could watch the passing of sea life he had never seen before. Taking in the sights as it all quickly passed him by, not even caring for his intrusion.

Minus one.

The siren who was lurking on the surface from before swiftly followed after him like a hungry wolf on the prowl, quickly circling Mydei to give him a few look overs. 

Mydei could only watch with owl-wide eyes, taking in how beautiful the creature was even in his clear distress on his face over Mydei’s arrival. Snow white hair, pale skin with just the slightest dusting of gold flaking his cheeks as if they were freckles before breaking into those pale scales he had easily seen before, a small black leather collar on his neck, deep blue piercing eyes that were focused on the ropes binding Mydei, webbed scaled fingers that were lightly dancing around him - removing pieces of jewelry abruptly quickly as well and tossing them to the side.

Mydei didn’t understand it.

If he didn’t know better, he could think the siren was trying desperately to save him from this unfortunate yet fated death.

He felt a pang of guilt as the siren almost looked elated with a smile and a twinkle in his eyes as he quickly cut away the last rope, which should easily have allowed Mydei to swim.

Only Mydei willed himself to look away from the siren and upwards at the now extremely distant sun. 

He had no idea how to swim - And even if he did, his lungs told him it was too late for that, and there was nothing to return to anyways. If anything - He would be branded a traitor for not allowing death to take him, for not allowing himself to be sacrificed for the ‘greater good’ of their people.

The siren on the other hand, did not seem to comprehend that, still appearing rather excited and bubbly as he fluttered about Mydei, moving to be in front of him and pointing upwards; As if he was directing Mydei to go get some air. Mydei instead only moved his hand forward, gently placing it onto the creature's head and petting the hair there that drifted in the ocean’s gentle current. Somewhat hoping that translated to a ‘thank you’ easily.

Apparently, it did not, instead he looked furious over the action, a quiet tone escaped his lips - Melodic, peaceful, and almost soothing compared to the noise from before. It completely betrayed the actions he was currently showcasing as he seemed to thrash his tail angrily. 

At least Mydei assumed that was a look of fury, Mydei wasn’t quite sure with his lack of air making it hard to think straight now and his lungs screaming for air. Mydei was very aware of the way the siren seemed to nudge at him in anger over that before circling Mydei again - Like he didn’t comprehend Mydei’s refusal to swim upwards.

Mydei wasn’t sure himself why he didn’t try very hard, honestly. He should have. 

And yet, as the siren moved towards his face, appearing utterly despairing in their expression; The creature swiftly forced something slimy into Mydei’s mouth, choking the last amount of air out of him and instead swallowing whatever that was. 

As his vision became spotted and blackening, he knew fully well his long-awaited fate had come.

Or well, that’s what he assumed as his lungs willingly sucked in water, craving it like it was air. Even as he lulled his head forward and continued guzzling down water, he couldn’t help but blink his eyes, attempting to rectify the blurriness within them - Realizing it was in fact acting like air somehow to his lungs.

“If I didn’t know better, it’s like you actually wanted to die.”

Mydei couldn’t help the way his head slowly turned towards the voice; Towards the siren to his right that was beaming at him, almost gleeful as he met Mydei’s gaze. He couldn’t even help the way he was steadily breathing in the water - no different than he would air. 

“I always thought this tradition was kind of cruel to the human.” 

The siren continued in such a tone that Mydei could only place it as pitying towards him, before placing an ice-cold, scaled, and webbed hand onto Mydei’s cheek, completely ignoring the way Mydei closed his eye on that side as he did so. The siren’s thumb slowly moved, and Mydei slowly made the realization he was tracing Mydei’s tattoo slowly.

“But you do have the markings they put on their sacrifices.. So pretty..”

Being told that almost made Mydei choke out a laugh - He probably would have if he wasn’t so utterly stunned by the creature. He knew his tattoos were given to him as some part of a ritual, but he had never figured they were the sign to the sirens of what he was for them. A branding of sorts it seemed.

“That must have been terrifying for you.. I’m sorry.”

Mydei’s eyes drifted at that, focusing on the translucent yet shimmering tail the man had - The base of it was white before breaking off into a light blue that glimmered and sparkled when the light from above reached it. A dazzling thing to see, and Mydei wasn’t quite sure how he was still alive to even see it.

The siren must have noticed his gaze on it, because the siren immediately moved it in front of himself, fanning it about almost like he was showing it off proudly to Mydei. 

“I’m Phainon! What’s your name?” The creature told him a bit too happily, still idly waving his tail there as he blinked expectantly at Mydei - Wide and gleaming, now completely almost lacking the predatory nature he had once gleaned from them. Some dark emotion still seemed to lurk the ocean-blue eyes there, something Mydei couldn’t place.

“.. Mydeimos.. Mydei.” 

Phainon seemed to beam at a whole new level beneath the depths as he flipped onto his back lazily, upside down as he stared at Mydei - And Mydei was unsure when the last time the creature had taken his eyes off of Mydei at all.

“Mydeimos.. Mydei… That’s a good name!” The happy trilling noise that left Phainon at that made Mydei almost huff out a laugh, almost. “Let’s have a good life together, Mydeimos Mydei!”

That laugh was stuck in his throat over that, those words were.. Odd. Mydei had come to terms that today was the day he died. That there wasn’t a day beyond this one, and now this siren was slowly circling Mydei again, making Mydei only able to watch him by turning his head slowly as he stayed in place. 

“Life.. Together?” Mydei echoed hollowly. 

“You’re my mate, after all!” Phainon’s tailfin at that wrapped around Mydei’s legs quickly, locking them together before Phainon abruptly pressed his head into the crook of Mydei’s neck. Like Mydei was supposed to actually understand what was happening here and not just stiffly trying to take everything in.

Those words didn’t really compute in his head at all - He had come to terms with dying. 

Yeah, sure.

He had not come to terms with.. Being a siren’s.. Mate?

“.. I’m your..” Mydei parroted, trailing off in utter shock and at that the siren only gave a loud bubbly laugh against the sensitive skin of Mydei’s neck, amused beyond belief over his confusion it seemed. 

“Oh!” Phainon broke away again at that, moving away with such a practiced ease that Mydei couldn’t help but be mesmerized with the way his body moved - The way his scales on his chest glimmered before snaking down into a long tail. Mydei would stare more, if not for the way Phainon clearly kept noticing and tried to appeal to him. It was somehow more embarrassing than Phainon already calling him his mate.. 

“So humans really don’t know why we demand someone, huh?” Phainon teased as he rolled a little, his tailfin spreading into a dazzling array of sparkled colors as he stretched himself, eyes tracking Mydei to make sure he was still watching - That predatory glint lingering within them again as he stared at Mydei, unblinking.

“I am Phainon, in human terms, I believe I am referred to as a ‘prince’.” Phainon continued his explanation, along with his clear flaunting of himself - obviously trying his best to keep Mydei’s attention solely on him. Which was remarkably easy, nothing else was near them and Mydei wasn’t exactly going to swim away from Phainon..

“We only pick a mate once, and our life spans are extremely long, as such the royal bloodline requires a human mate to keep the bloodline balanced, or something.” Mydei could only feel his jaw tense at that ‘or something’, noticeable by Phainon who laughed light-heartedly over it, still attempting to show off like some sort of peacock to Mydei. 

“.. Honestly, I kind of ignored that class, all I know is you’re my mate who I will have lots of spawn with!” Those words made the most sense to Mydei, at least the part of him in class, Phainon already did give off the type of vibes to zone out when he found something uninteresting..

It was still baffling to Mydei, however.. 

“Wouldn’t.. I just die and leave you alone for the rest of your life then, with that logic? Also I’m.. A man, I cannot give you ‘spawn’.” 

Many issues here. 

Many. 

Many issues..

Phainon seemed amused by that, making a show of his tail as he swished back to laying on his back in the sea’s water, eyes still keeping that dangerous tint to them as he focused wholly on Mydei; “No, no. You’ll turn into one of us too. The whole turning into a ‘siren’ thing will fix your lack of eggs, as well!”

Though Phainon said such words in a convincing and rather gentle tone - Mydei couldn’t quite believe him with how he watched the man roll his tongue against his lips while staring Mydei down. He was like ninety percent sure Phainon wanted to devour him whole, but the other ten percent remaining was completely befuddled by how Phainon was clearly trying to show off to him.

“.. Huh?” Was all Mydei managed instead, still in a daze and he somewhat stayed there suspended right where Phainon wanted him. At least, that’s what he assumed Phainon wanted from him as he seemed keen on fluttering around him. 

“Which part has confused you?” Phainon inquired sweetly, batting his eyes innocently as if he was more than willing to take all the time in the world to explain this to Mydei if he needed. Even readjusted himself to be laying on his stomach, staring at Mydei with his arms crossed in front of them - Head plopped on top of them as he stared holes into Mydei’s skull curiously.

“.. All of them?” Mydei painfully conceded, his eyes only blinking at the display before him as Phainon’s tail continued to flare out, doing his best to retain Mydei’s attention on it - Which well, embarrassingly it was working very well. Mydei mainly was staring at it out of pure confusion on if this was just his normal mannerisms, however.. 

“Oh..” Phainon mused in a tone that didn’t sound disappointed at all, instead still remaining staring at Mydei. Who.. Could only translate that as a sign to continue asking;  “How.. Am I going to turn into a siren?”

Phainon gave a small quiet hum at that before lashing his tail slightly, an action Mydei would have thought was akin to an angry cat if not for the way Phainon looked beyond pleased over Mydei asking that question. “Well. The kelp I made you eat let's humans breathe underwater, I did it to stop you from willingly drowning yourself to death - I would have been extremely upset at you if you had done that, by the way!” 

“But the longstanding side effect of using it does eventually turn humans into one of us and allow you to understand us! That’s why I tried to get you to the surface for air before force feeding you.” Phainon waved a hand languidly as he talked, causing bubbles to rise where his hand went, “Though, I wasn’t really sure how I was going to get all of that across to you without us speaking the same language, honestly..”

“So.. Sacrifices.. Aren’t killed.. And eaten?” Mydei felt beyond stupid, but he was still really stumped here - With the way Phainon was staring at him, every single bone in his body screamed that he was in danger. That this creature was luring him into a false sense of security before being eaten alive. 

Phainon looked almost taken aback by that before giving a small laugh however, one that was incredibly light for the topic; “What? No, You’re my mate!”

“I.. Am finding this hard to believe.” Mydei mumbled, his eyes drifting away from Phainon and towards the surface of the water - Towards the distant sun and merely blinked at it. “So it’s.. Basically an arranged marriage between kingdoms?”

“Yes!” Phainon hummed out, seeming extremely pleased over Mydei puzzling it together finally, albeit slowly, “Exactly!”

Mydei heaved out a deep sigh towards the sky above, a sigh he didn’t even know he had in him due to well.. Being under the water, and the fact he just had six hundred other current thoughts to try to figure out; “How do you know I’m actually from the royal bloodline and not some random man?”

“Easy!”

Phainon grabbed Mydei roughly at his spoken word, keeping his chin firmly held between clawed webbed hands as he forced Mydei to look back at Phainon - A crazed look just beneath the surface of those eyes was noticeable before Phainon immediately dove in for a rough and brutal kiss. There was no grace about it as Phainon thrashed his tail behind him, teeth clacking against Mydei’s, sharpened teeth grazing at his bottom lip as a tongue shoved its way into his mouth.

And well, Mydei had never been kissed underwater - The fact he found himself unable to breathe shouldn’t have been that odd, but his body had already grown used to swallowing down the water like air that his mind was reeling.

That feeling was only worsened as Phainon made sure to deepen the kiss like his life depended on it as his strange cold tongue roamed Mydei’s own mouth mercilessly - And Mydei had to fight the urge to gag over how far his somehow piercing cold tongue was reaching into him. The strangest part was how salty it tasted in his mouth as Phainon pushed into him. 

Mydei winced over it, moving a slowed hand in the waters to wrench at Phainon’s wrist - Gripping onto it firmly and that seemed to have done enough as Phainon immediately withdrew his tongue and released his chin, leaning away to only watch Mydei cough weakly. Even as Mydei fought to regain himself, he wasn’t blind to the way Phainon looked so proud while licking his lips, as if he had just claimed victory in some sort of competition over Mydei. 

“You’re their prince!” Phainon chirped happily, and Mydei could only take in breaths of.. Water, as he slowly met Phainon’s gaze. 

“.. How did a kiss tell you that?” Mydei wasn’t sure if his voice was actually hoarse beneath the noise of the ocean - Or if he only thought it may have been with the burning embarrassment on his cheeks over such a brutal and abrupt kiss. 

Phainon gave a warm chuckle at that, flaring at his tail again towards Mydei teasingly; “It didn’t! The kelp just would have killed you if you weren’t of their royal blood.”

Mydei could only knit his brows over that; “It was going to kill me?”

Phainon stared at him, twisting a bit in the murky blue waters before giving a small nod, but only innocently blinking at Mydei - Not understanding how he could have possibly have done anything wrong here. “Well. You were going to drown regardless - You would have died one way or another, worth a shot, right?”

“The kiss was just because I wanted to taste you while you’re still human!” 

Mydei could only feel his hand twitch as he motionlessly stared at Phainon - Wholly unsure of what he should even say to such a thing. Either things. 

He had expected to die.

He came to terms with it.

And now this.. Siren, was saying they were now ‘mates’ while shoving his tongue practically down Mydei’s throat.

What the hell was he supposed to think about any of it?

“Do you want to go to your new home?” Phainon asked in that same sing-song tone, chirpy, wholly unaware of Mydei’s inner turmoil, light and airy as he flicked his tail behind him. A movement that drew Mydei’s eyes immediately - Almost making him wonder if it was a way for them to distract prey before pouncing on them.

“My.. New home.” Mydei only echoed out slowly as his thoughts were already ramping up on the verge of being utterly baffling. Mates, and a new home. He was supposed to have drowned ten minutes ago, he was pretty sure of that much. 

“My home. Your home. Our home.” Phainon energetically nodded to him as he spoke, and Mydei had to swallow the fact that this creature really was somewhat cute - If he managed to ignore the way his eyes seemed to darken when Mydei so much as seemed slightly uninterested in him for the briefest moment. 

“.. Ah.” Mydei said rather dumbfoundedly, looking to see where Phainon was pointing to and well. He saw not a single thing but the fish floating and swimming within the depths. If anything, the sand seemed to slope downwards; As if Phainon was telling Mydei he was taking him even deeper into the abyssal depths of the sea. 

And that.. Was strange to Mydei to consider.

He would eventually turn into a siren like Phainon, and never walk on ground again.. Granted. That was better than dying, but it was still beyond baffling.

“It’s this way!” Phainon happily told him as he flapped his tailfin easily, a terrifying force of strength seemed to be behind it from how the current changed the way it was gently rocking Mydei. 

And well, Mydei could only stare after the man who had so abruptly pushed himself towards their destination, blinking wide-eyed at the space he had so effortlessly made between them both.

Mydei felt guilt bite into him over the way Phainon turned to make sure he was following him, only hesitating as he realized Mydei hadn’t moved at all - Not even a single attempt to follow. Not like he could even if he knew how to swim, was the siren insane? There was no way any man could keep up with him while swimming..

Mydei disregarded his own thoughts with a heavy sigh, eyes moving back to the waters that shimmered above distantly to avoid looking at those big pouty blue eyes; “I.. Do not know how to swim, Phainon.”

Phainon immediately moved to close the gap again, only confusedly tilting his head at that; “Huh?”

Well. That probably was a strange thing for a literal siren that only swims around and sings sailors to their doom and devours them to hear..

“I was.. Specifically kept away from water so that I would never learn how to swim.” Mydei explained easily, giving a deep sigh however over the way Phainon only seemed to inch ever closer at those words - Almost appearing very concerned over them.

“.. What?”

Mydei could only shrug and look away, not very willing to look at how increasingly distressed Phainon was appearing over this news. Mydei really didn’t get why he seemed so upset for Mydei’s sake, when Mydei himself came to terms with it many years ago. Though. Maybe the idea of being banned from the sea was a beyond heartbreaking concept for a creature that well, lived there.

“As you said.. There was a different expectation from me being thrown in the sea today.”

Phainon moved slightly, directly into Mydei’s line of sight with that same weird emotion buried within his eyes that Mydei couldn’t accurately read as Mydei felt an ounce of awe over how desperate he seemed to keep Mydei interested in him. 

“I see.. So those were indeed not just the ugliest ribbons I had ever seen adorning you..” Phainon muttered a bit darkly, quietly compared to his normal tone, almost as if he was saddened over the news.

But it was barely news, Mydei thought they already went over the whole ‘wanting him to drown’ thing earlier.

“The.. Ropes?” Mydei couldn’t help his small scoff he gave over that, something about the confusion was endearing even if Mydei didn’t think it added up quite correctly..

“I assumed due to the gold..” Phainon trailed off, his eyes still holding Mydei’s eye contact unblinking as he seemed to consider something.

“The jewelry were also offerings if I didn’t suffice.” Mydei told him before tearing his eyes away from those eerie piercing hungry pupils that seemed to desire to burrow into him. 

“How cruel..” Phainon mumbled before quickly moving, and Mydei almost assumed he was once again going to try to buy Mydei’s attention, only he swiftly moved himself through the water and to Mydei’s back. “Well! You’re perfect for me, Mydeimos Mydei! Let’s go home!”

“But-” 

Mydei tried to raise his complaints, only Phainon was already shuffling him around with his arms needily. Gentle in his ice cold touches, yet forcing Mydei into his arms in the style of a bridal carry, one that Mydei only allowed to happen. Mainly due to the whole ‘underwater’ thing. He wasn’t quite sure what else he even could do. 

Even if he refused Phainon carrying him like this or messing with him in general, what else was he to do? Swim up? But Phainon claims whatever he force fed Mydei would turn him into a siren eventually?

Thus.. Mydei only obeyed and allowed himself to be pliant and crumpled against Phainon’s chest and shoulder, almost shivering over how unnaturally cold he was for someone smiling so warmly at Mydei.

“I don’t know how to swim with those legs either, I’ll just carry you!”

Phainon was much too delighted as he said that; a sharp sounding noise akin to a purr quickly left his throat as Mydei’s head slapped into his shoulder. Mydei could only huff out lowly as Phainon immediately knocked his own head into the top of Mydei’s seemingly rubbing their heads together. 

“You smell good.” 

Mydei felt himself go rigid over that - For one; He wasn’t even aware sirens could smell underwater, secondly, he wasn’t even aware he would smell of anything but seasalt and sweat from being bound together in a hot room for so long. 

“What? Really?” Mydei asked, genuinely baffled by that as Phainon was quite obviously sniffing at him, tucking Mydei just a bit higher to sniff at him better as well. Something Mydei could only watch, completely flabbergasted over it. 

“It’s foreign to me, but you do smell rather nice. Sweet, even.”

“..Huh.” Mydei had no idea what to say to that, only blinking widely over how shameless this siren was. Or maybe they were all just this shameless - How was he to be able to say?

“Regardless! Let’s get you home, yes?” Phainon beamed at him as he said that, arms tightening Mydei closer to him if that was possible, and Mydei only found he had no idea what to ever say to this creature that had so quickly seemed to attach himself to him.

“.. Alright.”

“Feel free to hang onto me however you desire if you want, I won’t bite!” Phainon told him, rather obviously giddy in his voice over the mere idea of that; “In fact, I’d heavily prefer it if you did cling onto me.”

“.. I’m not doing that.” Mydei mumbled quietly, he wasn’t sure how much face he could save by this point - But he was taking what he could.

“Awe..”

Mydei did however turn his head facing his own knees as Phainon lashed his tail and propelled them onwards at a high speed. Too fast - Much faster than he had ever moved by far, and it was simply powered by that lone, long tail fin. His eyes only trailed Phainon’s neck slightly, taking in the sight of the sun tattoo on his neck that seemed to glow faintly - Mydei found that rather humorous for a siren to have.

They certainly didn’t see the sun down here.

He didn’t even know how to tell the time anymore, only vaguely aware of the way the waters seemed to change hues - darker, deeper into the unknown to him.

The only thing he would know here is Phainon, and that sounded extremely worrisome to him.

Mydei could only blink as Phainon slowed himself, at least he was pretty sure he did with the rate of water brushing against his skin slowing dramatically - With that, Mydei turned his head to focus on whatever Phainon was taking him to. 

“A reef?” Mydei blinked at it, it was vibrant. So very full of life and colors deep below the waters yet still glowing - the way it was beyond giant was baffling to him. 

“Mhm.” Phainon hummed out, still diving towards it; And Mydei didn’t miss the way his hold on Mydei tightened. “It’s quite deep, humans die coming this deep so it’s very safe.”

“Er..”

“You’re not quite human anymore, Mydeimos Mydei.”

“Right.. It’s just one of those, by the way.”

Phainon cocked his head to the side at that, not stopping his movements however, “One of what?”

“Mydeimos or Mydei. Mydei is just a nickname my friends call me, Mydeimos is my full name..”

Phainon stalled at that for a second before giving a warm laugh, one that vibrated Phainon’s chest and Mydei could feel it; “Alright, Mydei.”

Mydei couldn’t help the way his head tilted upwards at the first sign of another fin passing by in a hurry - A flash of color as it passed. Another flash to the side drew his head again, still blinking as Phainon effortlessly weaved past coral, not so much as even giving a glance to the other sirens quickly passing by.

“There’s.. A lot of sirens, huh?” Mydei found himself dumbly asking as his eyes followed another that met his own gaze - Only to quickly turn away abruptly, as if avoiding his eyes at all costs. 

“Yep!” Phainon’s voice was clipped, no longer light and chirper, now rough around the edges and bordering on darkened. Mydei had to suppress the desire to question him on that directly, instead opting for a second route. 

“.. They don’t seem happy to see us - Or is it just me they're unhappy to see?”

Phainon gave a warm chuckle over that question, still diving even lower into the depths beneath the coral, and Mydei couldn’t help but look upwards past Phainon at the vibrancy they were leaving behind; “Both of us, probably.”

Mydei clicked his tongue at that, eyes moving to meet Phainon’s, for once noticing the way his face didn’t seem as happy-go-lucky nearly at all anymore. A full blown scowl had replaced it.

“You’re an unpopular prince? They’re.. Avoiding looking at you.” Mydei inquired, drifting his eyes away from it. There was clearly a reason for the sudden switch of emotions. 

“It’s not really that, I’ll just snap their fins for looking at you. They know this.”

Mydei felt himself go rigid in Phainon’s tight grip on him, mulling that answer over in his mind before landing on the most useful question he could come up with in this scenario; “.. Huh?”

“You’re mine, after all.” Phainon said remarkably flatly, like it was the most logical answer; “So they should be taught to keep their eyes to themselves. The breaking of their fins is the least I will do to them.”

Mydei quieted at that, that was the most insane thing he had ever heard from a person he had just met on the same day. He couldn’t help but let his mind wander back to the sparse books he had dared read about sirens in his pastime when he desired to learn about how he would die. Sirens  were frightening creatures, luring in people with their voice and whispers of sweet nothings before drowning them and eating them - bones and all.

If anything, it felt like Phainon was still working on the step of ‘sweet nothings’ - Whenever the hell the drowning and eating him was supposed to happen was a mystery to Mydei by now. 

Though, he was sufficiently lacking in the field of offering Mydei things he would want - Maybe due to the fact Mydei had already been dumped into the sea. 

The other things he had read..

“That’s.. Are sirens actually territorial?”

Phainon gave him a rather knowing smile at that, beaming and almost excited by the question as he tilted his head slightly to look at Mydei in the eyes; “Extremely! Why do you ask?”

“.. No reason.” Was all Mydei could manage.

This siren had for sure lost his marbles.

Mydei jolted slightly when Phainon abruptly turned, diving into a small crevice that was barely even noticeable to Mydei before immediately dropping Mydei. Well, Dropping wasn’t the right term since they were in the sea, but he certainly did floor down into something soft. 

“.. I can’t see.” Mydei mumbled with the distant light of the coral now gone and out of sight, Mydei was now instead tucked away in whatever Phainon had dragged him quickly into. His fingers timidly touched whatever was beneath him, soft, squishy, it was a plant of some kind, but Mydei would never be able to discern what it was with no ability to see. 

And Mydei only could find himself staring Phainon in the eyes, sharp blue eyes that seemed to glow lightly in the dark - transfixed wholly on Mydei with that same look of a predator beneath them. Maybe even amplified by how he assumed Mydei couldn’t see his eyes.

For once, Mydei hesitated in the realization that he should be cold down here - numb and weak. But Phainon was right.. He was becoming no longer human. The chill of the depths wasn’t even biting at his skin nearly as much as it should be.

“Oh!” Mydei couldn’t see Phainon, but he certainly could hear him. Hear how happy he was in his voice alone. Even worse was how he could watch those eyes not change at all, unmatching with how joyful he sounded- Only staring Mydei down who found himself looking away from them; “Let’s feed you more, then.”

He was very happy to hurry Mydei into being a siren like him, it seemed.

“That speeds the transformation along, doesn't it?” Mydei asked for clarification, only able to hear the hum of the sea and Phainon’s tail swishing quietly as he moved, the current of the space Mydei was in drifting along at Phainon’s whims - swaying Mydei slightly as he waited. 

“Yep! I harvested quite a lot of it waiting for you.” Phainon hummed out, and Mydei nearly jolted as a cold hand touched his lower back on his spine, seeping through the thin white shirt he had been dressed in like it was nothing as Phainon pressed.

“Waiting for me? How long did you wait?” Mydei asked, pausing as he felt something reach his lips, slimy and painfully cold. Something he couldn’t see yet again, and still, he opened his mouth willingly and Phainon gently pushed it in. 

Flavorless, but he swallowed it regardless, earning a very pleased hum from Phainon at his right - Those blue eyes completely unblinking as he watched every move Mydei took. 

“My entire life.” Phainon answered easily, like it was just an average question he was asked all of the time. And maybe it was. 

“Your entire life..?” Mydei echoed, wincing slightly over more of it being forced into his mouth when he opened to speak; He swallowed it once more without complaint, only huffing over the way Phainon was so greedy and quick about it.

“Of course! I am only allowed to mate with a human, and you were prophesied to be mine; So I waited for you.” Phainon explained a bit too happily beside him, and Mydei wished he could look at the man to be able to tell what emotions his face outside of those eerie eyes was giving away. 

He clearly had two different personalities within him, the one that seemed overly friendly towards Mydei, and something much, much darker beneath the surface of his ocean blue colored eyes that were watching Mydei like a starving wolf.

“My patience did run thin, however.” Phainon conceded, sighing dramatically as he moved just a bit closer to Mydei, something he was only aware of with how Phainon seemed to radiate a chill from his body. “So many cycles and never even a glance or acknowledgement from my mate..”

“Only to learn now that they were keeping him from me..” Mydei felt himself sit up slightly at that, over the way his voice sounded jagged again, like he was furious but desperately trying to keep that at bay - Desperately trying not to allow Mydei to see it. Even though Mydei quite literally could not see currently.

“Is that why other sirens started attacking our kingdom more?” Mydei pressed, disregarding that hidden ire that Phainon was trying to shovel away and hide, only to be rewarded with a cold hand pushing more of whatever that was into his mouth. A happy trill from Phainon came immediately when Mydei swallowed, making his skin burn with wonder of how closely Phainon was watching him currently. 

“Maybe. I have been quite.. Irritable lately!”

Mydei didn’t dare question what this man meant by irritable, if anything, he had a sneaking suspicion that Phainon was absolutely dangerous. Not even really ‘sneaking’. He had flat out said he would hurt his own fellow sirens over Mydei already..

“Sorry for making you wait..” Mydei mumbled, not really quite sure what else to say to that, and only immediately stiffening as he felt cold hands brush through his hair gently, slowly, an odd tingly feeling in the silence of the sea depths with almost no gravity affecting his strands. 

“No need to apologize.. You didn’t know, Mydei..” Phainon was soft at that, no hint of malice or the way his tone became clipped sometimes, apparently having a weak spot for Mydei. One that he couldn’t quite rationalize, but maybe that just came from how long he had waited for Mydei.

Mydei moved at that, moved to rub at his eyes with the back of his hands dully as his vision blurred; adapted to the darkness around him. 

But it burned.

It stung like hell.

“Stop that..” Phainon quietly hissed at him, a tone that sounded foreign as he batted Mydei’s hands from Mydei’s own eyes. Mydei could only knit his brows in confusion, in slight agitation, before Phainon’s own hands replaced Mydei’s gently. 

Cold.

Soothing.

Probably even an endearing act to think about if his eyes didn’t currently burn like hell.

“Better?”

Mydei gave a small laugh over it, over how stupid this must look. “It is, actually. Thanks.”

Phainon didn’t miss a beat however, instead a tinge of curiosity seeping into his tone; “Does it hurt?” 

“It burns a little.”

It was as if Mydei had gotten shampoo in his eyes, but much worse, a lingering feeling that didn’t seem to ebb, the only safety he had currently was Phainon’s hands working as ice to soothe them..

“Sorry..” Phainon hushedly mumbled, and Mydei couldn’t help but find that funny as well, giving a slow and quiet chuckle. 

“I expected you to eat me earlier today. Not end up being protective of me.” His life was truly beyond ironic now, from sacrificial lamb to being coddled by the ‘monster’ he was sent to satiate with his life. 

Though, in a way, he guessed he was still doing just that.

“My poor confused Mydei..” Phainon cooed at his side, soft and much too kind of a creature Mydei expected all his life to shred him into pieces, “It’s okay..”

Mydei wasn’t even sure how long he sat there with his eyes closed, letting Phainon act as a pack of ice as he listened to the sounds around him. It was silent - horribly so, but expected from the way they were so very far beneath the waves. The other thing he could hear so distantly were the songs. 

The other sirens distantly singing, so quietly and far, yet it still itched at Mydei’s mind if he even tried to zero in on them at all.

“Do you not sing much like other sirens?” Mydei idly asked, curious over it - He had only really clearly heard Phainon sing in the forewarned ‘siren’ song once as he was thrown into the depths while bound. The other time was just the tiniest noise when he was drowning, now feeling slightly guilty over knowing now it was out of pure sorrow and dread over the idea of Mydei dying.

“Don’t want to risk hurting your ears.” Phainon simply stated, “I’ll sing plenty of songs with you when you are a siren, too.” 

“What.. Would you have done if I had drowned?” Mydei was curious. Beyond curious about it.

If the current issues with the sirens were due to Phainon simply being impatient about Mydei not being thrown into the sea to him; What would Phainon had done to them if they had actually drowned Mydei? If Mydei had not continued to breathe? 

This creature had a dark side, one that seemed well locked behind doors he was straining to keep closed around Mydei.

But that only made Mydei so much more interested in opening that box... 

‘Curiosity killed the cat’ is a saying for a reason after all. 

Mydei physically felt Phainon tense over the question, over the idea of Mydei dying, even his hands seemed strained as he forced out a hollow laugh; “That’s not a very fun idea to consider.. I don’t want to think about that right now.. I only just finally found you..”

“.. Alright, sorry.” Mydei said hoarsely, now feeling a pang of guilt gnawing into him over it, over the way Phainon seemed so earnestly upset over even considering such a thing. It was hard to wrap his head around; But it made more sense to consider Phainon said he had waited for Mydei. Longing for this day to come, while Mydei dreaded it. Both for completely different reasons, yet meeting at the end of it.

“It’s fine! I’m not angry!” Phainon was quick to reassure him lightly, before scoffing, “At least.. Not at you, Mydei!”

Phainon didn’t give him a chance to really think about that ‘not at you’, instead continuing on swiftly; “Would you like to try to adjust to the light again?”

“Sure.” 

Phainon slowly removed his hands at that, as if unsure if he really should listen to Mydei instead of simply latching onto him. Mydei only found himself blinking hard, many times as he tried to focus.

“If you want my hands back, let me know! I don’t mind at all!”

Mydei continued his blinking, trying to clear whatever was fogging his sight. He could see now - not very well, but he could clearly see the radiant glowing man before him that had his head tilted like a puppy. Mydei could only blink at the way his floaty white locks seemed so beautiful in the dim lighting - and the way his sun tattoo seemed to give off a small amount of gold light as well.

Phainon was eerily beautiful - akin to a ghost in the dim lighting in the depths, porcelain and borderline terrifying with his sharp searching eyes. 

And yet, Mydei couldn’t look away from him.

“It’s alright.. I think it’s fine now.” Mydei reassured him, leaning back slightly as Phainon immediately stuck his hand towards him again. 

“Can you see well?” Phainon inquired in a rather soothing tone, waving his fingers in front of his face before sticking a few of them down, “How many fingers am I holding up, Mydei?”

Mydei had to bite his tongue at that, fighting the urge to slap the siren over the side of his head as Mydei pushed out a small huff of laughter over how childish this seemed. 

It’s hazy, dark, and kind of hard to truly see much and yet; “.. Two.”

He could at least make out fingers two inches from his nose, if anything..

“Lucky guess!” Phainon’s delighted voice rang out to him, though Mydei only found his own eyes looking past Phainon and instead around where Phainon had ushered him away. 

It was a cave, yes, a small hole in the literal wall beneath the reef, buried beneath the coral and hidden away - But it was obviously lived in. It was clearly Phainon’s home of sorts - the most interesting of which being a wall cut away in the cave walls, one that made Mydei wonder just how strong those hands of Phainon’s were with how clearly carved out it was.

The items on the wall were most interesting to him, they were clearly human knicknacks. Neatly placed and organized, a baffling thing to see within the depth - the less baffling thing was Phainon moving slightly to try vying for Mydei’s attention once again rather obviously.

Mydei gave an exasperated sigh at that, over his somehow needy, pet dog, who was a fish that had abruptly entered his life.

“What are those, Phainon?” Mydei attempted to redirect the puppy’s attention, moving to point a finger around him, easily working as Phainon quickly looked over his shoulder at what had captivated Mydei’s attention over him.

“Mm?” Phainon hummed out before instantly jerking his head back to Mydei at his abrupt realization, like it only just hit him Mydei actually knows what they were.“Oh! Actually, wouldn’t you know better than I?” 

“I just like collecting the interesting things humans drop sometimes..” Phainon told him, almost looking rather excited as he looked at the shelf again, and even with hazy blurred vision, Mydei could tell he was slightly embarrassed by this topic. 

Mydei couldn’t rationalize why, humans kept siren scales after all. This felt like a level of fair trade, so instead he just huffed slightly. “With how you disregarded the jewelry they put on me, I didn’t consider you cared for this type of stuff.”

Phainon tossed his head towards Mydei, focusing wholly on him again and giving a click of his tongue, Mydei almost would have thought he was angered with that movement if not for the smile on his lips. “Well. My mate was literally drowning in front of me, it wasn’t really the time to care about shiny objects..”

“Besides! You still have the one in your fin and the one in your hair! Saved two of them.” Phainon said with a slow curt nod, as if it was a fair trade.

Mydei blinked at that. Very slowly.

“.. Fin?”

Phainon reached towards him at that word, gently grazing against his cheek as he rather delicately grabbed onto Mydei’s earlobe. Tapping idly at the golden jewelry still pierced into his ear there. Mydei couldn’t help but scoff over the action, the pure wonder that seemed to grace Phainon’s actions with Mydei involved.

“This.” Phainon chirped out, his rather happy tone returning, and Mydei couldn’t help but wonder how that gold even felt in his hands that were covered in scales.

 Instead of asking, Mydei only found himself giving a small laugh. “Oh, That’s my ear.”

“Your ear.” Phainon withdrew his hand at that, moving to cross his arms over his bare chest before giving a quiet trilling noise, one that Mydei couldn’t read the emotion behind at all; “I don’t know too much about humans, it's hard to learn about you when we do not speak the same language..”

Mydei found himself choking back a laugh over that word - The fact sirens also lead humans to their doom and devour them in bloody waters also probably doesn’t really aid in the public relations field. Not that Mydei would say that to this siren prince, no matter how he claimed to be Mydei’s mate currently.. Maybe that was a talk to have months later if he lived that long.

“That’s fine. I don’t know much about sirens either outside..” Mydei chose to say instead, trailing off as he tried to think about what he did know about them. 

“Outside?”

“Mainly just how dangerous you are.” Mydei answered honestly, moving to copy Phainon’s pose of crossing his arms over his chest with a heavy sigh. Nothing in his life had prepared him for having to explain humans to a siren; In fact, everything in his life had prepared him to be eaten by a siren.

And now that very siren was staring at him, doe-eyed and tail practically wagging like a dog when Mydei so much as looked his way. 

“Oh.” Phainon however did sound a bit sullen by that, “Do you fear me?”

Mydei uncrossed an arm to wave it dismissively lazily, a teasing smirk creeping its way onto his face over the siren’s curious nature; “After learning you hoard antiques? Not quite.”

“Harsh!” Phainon lashed his tail almost playfully at that, his smile beaming and Mydei couldn’t help but notice just how truly sharp his teeth were - Jagged in his mouth. Terrifying, if not for the fact Phainon had already shoved his tongue down Mydei’s throat.. 

Phainon on the other hand had no idea about those thoughts, instead looking to that carved shelf behind him once more before looking at Mydei with a twinkle in his eyes; “Do you know anything about them?”

“Wanting to learn about them?” Mydei asked, a genuine bit of surprise seeping into his words over it. Truthfully - he didn’t think sirens viewed humans as much more than livestock that sometimes toppled into the sea over their enchanting songs. He guessed it was fair, he was finding himself more and more curious about the siren himself as he sat here staring at the creature.

It probably was very baffling to see an entire life beyond the waters just beyond your reach that sometimes lost cargo into the open waters.

Mydei supposed he had the best of both worlds even if he was killed by Phainon now; Seeing both worlds with his own eyes. 

“Yes!” And Mydei wished he could say he was immune to how rather cute Phainon acted towards him sometimes, nodding his head quickly with wide eyes as he said such a simple admission. 

“Alright. Bring them here.” Mydei instructed him almost lazily, uncrossing his arms to lay on them a bit behind him, eyes flickering to the soft plant beneath him for once as he laid back. Seaweed? Maybe? Mydei didn’t really have a frame of reference; So he couldn’t quite say for certain. 

“Not going to try to learn to swim?” Phainon teased, though he was already obeying and gently moving towards his collection of ‘oddities’, and even with Mydei’s poor vision in the dark he couldn’t help but linger his eyes on the siren as he turned his back for once - focusing on gathering whatever items he wanted to show and ask Mydei about.

“Right before I turn into a siren like you and have to relearn swimming? I’ll pass.” Mydei huffed out, keenly watching as Phainon seemed indecisive over which items to show Mydei. Picking some of them up and clearly inspecting them before setting them back down - and Mydei almost felt like Phainon was embarrassed over this. 

Insane thing to be embarrassed about considering all the other things Phainon had already said to Mydei, but, fine. 

“Fair enough.” Phainon hummed out before seemingly deciding on something, picking them up before swiftly turning back to Mydei with a flourish of his tail;  “These. I’ve found so many of them with different little pictures.”

Phainon’s words left his lips so quickly, his eyes avoiding Mydei’s own gaze as he returned to Mydei’s side, making Mydei really come to terms that Phainon was deeply shy over this. Was it not common for a siren to collect things like this?

Was Phainon considered a hoarder in his society? 

Mydei blinked as Phainon held out his hand before slowly extending his own beneath his, cocking his head to the side as he watched Phainon tenderly press something cold into his palm.

Mydei brought it closer to himself, inspecting the ever familiar silver metal before twirling it slightly between his fingers; “Oh. This is just currency for bartering.”

“Currency.” Phainon repeated as he lowered himself slightly, moreso to be on eye level with Mydei who merely chose to ignore the encroaching siren in favor of looking at the metal.

“Yeah. It’s called a coin, each of them means a different amount of currency.” Mydei explained, extending his hand again to give it back to Phainon, suppressing a small shiver over the chill of Phainon’s hands brushing his own as he took it back. 

Phainon muttered quietly, eyes focusing on the item he could now place as a ‘coin’; “Sounds complicated.”

Mydei could only shrug, his eyes trailing the length of Phainon’s body lazily, never quite adapting to the fact he was talking to a siren, let alone one that claimed to be his ‘mate’ and a ‘prince’. 

“Not really, easy to get the hang of really since it’s part of daily life, but judging by the vase over there; You probably would spend your money on fakes in another life.” Mydei teased, once again moving his eyes behind Phainon to blink at a white intricate vase, one that Mydei almost felt baffled over the idea of it surviving a fall into the depths. 

White, a delicate blue design painted across the surface to form flowers that Mydei could only think were lilies. He wasn’t well versed in flowers, though. 

“Fakes? That’s a very real object, I assure you of that much, Mydei..” Phainon said without a single hint of jesting, like Mydei’s sentence was beyond perplexing. And, well. It probably was.

Mydei gave a small laugh, looking away from the vase with a shake of his head, he would have to concede here. Explaining ‘fakes’ versus ‘real’ to Phainon would be an insane task to take on. “.. You got me there, I guess.”

Phainon didn’t miss a beat however, his tailfin splaying out behind him, clearly using it to point at it; “What is it used for?”

“Uh.. Sometimes people put things in them, but what you’re doing with it is also a common use.”

Phainon scrunched up his face at that, clearly not understanding that meaning at all; “What I’m doing with it..? It’s just sitting there.”

Mydei felt himself bite back a deep sigh, if anything, this siren was lucky he was rather bafflingly cute appearance wise and personality wise. Minus when Mydei had the sinking feeling of dread over Phainon’s mood abruptly swapping..  

“Yeah. For decoration in your home.” Mydei mumbled out, opting to disregard his feelings of uncertainty for now - Phainon didn’t seem to have any plans of letting that personality leak out too much for Mydei to see at the least. 

Not yet, anyway.

“Oh!” Phainon moved quickly however, turning away and back to the shelf to gather a new thing, quickly dashing back to Mydei’s side who only swayed slightly over Phainon kicking his tail towards him in swift movements. “Okay, wait. What about these?”

Mydei blinked at the object in Phainon’s hands, he didn’t even really need to see them closer - and yet Phainon happily offered them to him. 

“Glasses.” Mydei told him quietly, before inspecting them slightly. They were high quality, that’s for sure. One lens was broken and cracked - But the other remained in good condition, the smooth bronze of the framework was still well kept as well. Phainon most likely treasured these things, it seemed. 

“They’re to help people see.” Mydei mumbled, placing them on his own face slowly as if to show an example of it, only to blink over how blurry it abruptly made his vision before quickly removing them as Phainon watched his every move. 

“Do all humans have bad vision?” Phainon asked innocently as Mydei handed the glasses back to him, making Phainon hum over it, leaning slightly to copy Phainon in looking at the metal of it and then the lenses. 

Mydei huffed a laugh over the question; “.. Not all, just the unfortunate.”

“Oh. Do you?” Phainon seemed a bit sullen as he asked, but Mydei only shrugged his shoulders, watching Phainon’s scaled and slightly clawed fingers twist at the metal gentle - twirling the glasses a bit idly as he studied at Mydei. 

“Sometimes.. I can see far away, but struggle up close to see some things - I need them for reading.”

Phainon seemed to consider that for a second before giving a low hum, blue eyes for once fully drifting from Mydei to instead focus on the glasses in his hands as he spoke; “Really? How interesting..”

Mydei had to give it to him, he did at least sound like he actually was interested in Mydei’s explanation. 

“.. I guess I won’t have that issue soon?” Mydei said mainly in jest, partly due to the fact that he still was reeling over.. Everything.

“Nope!” Phainon didn’t seem to mind or notice however, abruptly turning away again to return the glasses to their rightful spot before swiftly returning - Phainon moved at speeds that Mydei almost thought he acted as if Mydei may swim away if he looked away for too long. That feeling was only aided by how those glowing blue eyes would glance over his shoulder, making sure Mydei was still sitting there. 

Phainon lowered himself slightly, handing Mydei something yet again. “What about this?”

This one was more interesting in the way that it was heavy. 

A solid golden pen. Expensive.

And utterly useless now that it had been buried at the bottom of the depths, safe in the clutches of a curious siren.

“A pen.. For writing.” Mydei said with a low hum as he felt the weight of it - Even in the water he could tell this was more of a decoration than actual penmanship. It was much too heavy to be comfortable. 

“Why did you collect these?” Mydei asked blankly, mainly because most of these seemed useless to Phainon outside of just wondering about humans. Though, it probably was just that simple. 

“I was curious.” Phainon practically purred out and Mydei could only flick his eyes to look at the siren who seemed more interested in Mydei than the item he was actually supposed to tell him about. 

“Curious?” 

“About you and your life - But I couldn’t see or talk to you..” Phainon confessed, his tail swishing a bit solemnly as he spoke before he immediately perked up with his own thoughts; “So, I collected them! In the hope that one day you would do this!”

Mydei’s eyes moved back to that pen, pieces ‘do this’ together slowly in his own mind; “.. Explain them to you?”

“Yes!” 

Mydei couldn’t help but realize how.. Clear, his vision was becoming as he blinked at the small golden pen, uncapping it and closing it slowly before handing it back off to Phainon.

Just how well he was able to see Phainon as he moved back to the shelf - Instead moving his eyes to really take in just where they were with the acknowledgement. The above entrance was the only real light, and even then that was barely anything compared to what Mydei was used to, just the faintest glimmer of a reflection from the surface waves miles and miles above.

Hell. It probably wasn’t even that and was instead whatever life was making the reef seem to glow with life - Mydei didn’t know. 

The small cave was remarkably barren, save for the makeshift bed and the small amount of rather human items Phainon collected - It didn’t look lived in at all. If anything, Mydei had the sneaking suspicion Phainon was hiding him here, away from wherever he actually actively lived. This was more of a secret ‘lair’ than anything else. A place he would call cold and damp - if a cave submerged completely underwater could ever be considered damp. 

“Do you live here?”

Phainon was silent for a moment at that question before giving a small shallow laugh; “Not quite, we’re still a bit away from home.”

“Huh..” Mydei murmured, eyes still taking in the sight of the small dug out cave. It did make more sense that it was just some spot Phainon had to hide away in sometimes. And with how quiet it was here, the title of ‘prince’ was a curious one if it really was about five sirens in total Mydei saw. 

“I wanted to keep you nice and safe before you turn, then we can go into the actual city..” Phainon trailed off, his tail thumping into the floor akin to an angry rabbit almost at his own thoughts, “The other sirens you saw are royal guards, no one else is allowed near here.”

“Oh..” Mydei had nothing to say to that, he couldn’t really find it in him to question Phainon more on it. After all, if the sirens sang, Mydei would easily fall under their influence, which was probably what Phainon was aiming to avoid happening to him.

“.. How long does becoming a siren usually take?” Mydei drifted his gaze back to Phainon, to the siren who only stared at him like he was some type of treasure to be hoarded away as he came back once more - Hands empty this time with nothing more to ask Mydei about. 

Mydei wished he hadn’t been staring Phainon in the eyes however, because nothing could have prepared him for the answer Phainon conjured up immediately to his question. 

“Depends on how much you ingest! Once you fully turn, I will make sure to thoroughly breed you, rest assured!” Phainon said, and Mydei could only choke slightly on his own tongue that felt like cotton over that, over the way Phainon had said it so earnestly - So happily, like it was the easiest answer to ever pop into his little siren head.

“.. Huh?” Mydei felt the word tumble from his lips without much of a thought. Only slowly able to screw his face into one of confusion over those words. Thoroughly.. Breed him..?
